conventions.convention: Double complexes are anticommuting: h²=0, v²=0 and h∘v+v∘h=0; the total differential is h+v with no extra sign. A commuting convention must first apply the twist ṽ=(-1)^p v, as in the remark.
Sum and product totalisations exist only under the stated diagonal coproduct/product hypotheses; they are compared by the canonical map and agree exactly on finite diagonals.

Row filtration cuts off the vertical index (F^row_s T_n = ⊕_{p+q=n, q≤s} C_{p,q}) and takes horizontal homology first, with E^0_{p,q}=C_{q,p} and E^1_{p,q}=H^h_q(C_{*,p}); the column filtration is the transpose (E^0_{p,q}=C_{p,q}, E^1_{p,q}=H^v_q(C_{p,*})), and both have d^r of bidegree (-r,r-1).

An exact couple is bigraded: page r has deg i=(1,-1), deg j=(1-r,r-1), deg k=(-1,0); initial means r=1 with j of degree (0,0), and the generated spectral sequence starts at E^1, not E^0 (derivation sends r to r+1 with deg j'=(-r,r)).
On this page regular means two-sided eventual vanishing of both incident differentials; the one-sided Stacks notions are named outgoing regularity and incoming regularity separately.

Weak convergence requires specified E^∞_{p,q} ≅ F_pH_{p+q}/F_{p-1}H_{p+q} isomorphisms induced by actual cycles; strong convergence adds two-sided regularity and an exhaustive, separated, complete target filtration, and never identifies the unfiltered target with its associated graded.

The five-term sequences are stated with normalized filtration endpoints: cohomological F^0H^n=H^n, F^{n+1}H^n=0 and no terminal surjectivity onto H^2; homological F_{-1}H_n=0, F_nH_n=H_n and no initial injectivity H_2→E^2_{2,0}.

Singular cochains are Hom(C_n(X;Z),G) for n≥0 and 0 for n<0 with the positive coboundary δφ=φ∘∂ (no degree sign); they are arbitrary functions on the unnormalised simplex set and need not have finite support.

Mayer-Vietoris difference sign: the 8A topological sequence uses β([u],[v])=u|-v| (U minus V) with the positive extension-differential connector; the 9A real/smooth track uses i(c)=(-c,c) and β(u,v)=v|-u|, whose connector is minus the AT connector.

UCT: Ext is computed from a length-one projective resolution of the first variable, β is Kronecker evaluation, the sequence is natural and the splitting is only nonnatural (after choices); AC is assumed for arbitrary-rank projections.
Künneth: the left arrow is the actual singular cross product (shuffle signs on generators), the right term is Tor_1 of the homology modules, and no splitting of the sequence is chosen.

The additive cohomology cross product is defined on homogeneous cochains by J(φ,ψ) supported in bidegree (p,q) with no extra sign, has δJ(φ,ψ)=J(δφ,ψ)+(-1)^p J(φ,δψ), and is additive only; cup products are not defined here.

Fibration conventions: Hurewicz tests all spaces, Serre tests disks D^n, no surjectivity is imposed; the connecting map fixes the terminal point (∂_p[γ]=[e_0]·[γ]^{-1} in π_0(F)) with loop products traversed left-to-right, and π_0 terms are only pointed sets.

Bundle charts are ordinary product charts; numerable means the data include a support-subordinate locally finite partition of unity, and the Hurewicz conclusion for numerable bundles is proved under AC by well-ordering the finite chart words.

Smooth singular simplices are defined by a target-valued smooth extension on an open neighbourhood in the affine hyperplane A^k (not merely separate smoothness of faces); constant and degenerate simplices are retained in all complexes.

Smooth/continuous comparison is the restriction map ρ_M (evaluate a continuous cochain on smooth simplices); the isomorphism theorem assumes AC_ω and, for boundary targets, pushes finite compact sets into the interior instead of prescribing boundary faces during smoothing.

Connection conventions: ∇:Γ(E)→Ω¹(M;E)=Γ(Hom(TM,E)) with ∇(fs)=df⊗s+f∇s; frame convention e'=eA, ∇_X(eu)=e(X(u)+ω(X)u) and ω'=A^{-1}ωA+A^{-1}dA; existence of a connection for an arbitrary bundle is proved with full AC via partitions of unity.

Christoffel/Levi-Civita: ∇_{∂_i}∂_j=Σ_k Γ^k_{ij}∂_k with the first lower index the differentiating direction and no symmetry asserted; torsion T(X,Y)=∇_XY-∇_YX-[X,Y]; 2g(∇_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z) with K=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)-g(X,[Y,Z])+g(Y,[Z,X])+g(Z,[X,Y]); torsion-free is equivalent to symmetric coordinate symbols.

Along-curve conventions: sections of γ*E, D_tV=(γ*∇)_{∂/∂t}V, parallel means D_tV=0; piecewise smooth means continuous with one-sided derivatives at corners; a singleton has identity transport; concatenation traverses the first curve first and composes transports in the order P_{γ_2*γ_1}=P_{γ_2}∘P_{γ_1}.

Choice boundaries are declared per item: AC for the tower/Delta lemmas, the UCT and Künneth arbitrary-rank cycle projections, the numerable-bundle well-order and connection existence; AC_ω for the Whitney smoothing and the countable-union/exhaustion globalization; the double-complex, exact-couple, Mayer-Vietoris, fibration and supplied-connection arguments are choice-free.
conventions.fixed_by: def-axiom-of-choice and def-countable-choice as cited by each item (e.g. thm-complete-exhaustive-filtered-complex-convergence-criterion, thm-topological-universal-coefficient-short-exact-sequence-for-cohomology, thm-numerable-fiber-bundles-are-hurewicz-fibrations, thm-smooth-singular-chains-compute-singular-homology, thm-every-smooth-vector-bundle-admits-a-connection)

load_bearing.statement: A homological double complex in an abelian category consists of objects C_{p,q} (p,q in Z) and morphisms h_{p,q}:C_{p,q}→C_{p-1,q}, v_{p,q}:C_{p,q}→C_{p,q-1} satisfying h_{p-1,q}h_{p,q}=0, v_{p,q-1}v_{p,q}=0 and h_{p,q-1}v_{p,q}+v_{p-1,q}h_{p,q}=0; first quadrant means C_{p,q}=0 for p<0 or q<0.

C^n(X;G)=Hom_Z(C_n(X;Z),G) for n≥0 and 0 for n<0; δ^nφ=φ∘∂_{n+1} (positive convention, zero for n<0); a cochain is equivalently an arbitrary function on the singular simplex set, with no finite-support requirement.

A page-r homological exact couple is families D_{p,q}, E_{p,q} with i_{p,q}:D_{p,q}→D_{p+1,q-1}, j_{p,q}:D_{p,q}→E_{p+1-r,q+r-1}, k_{p,q}:E_{p,q}→D_{p-1,q} satisfying im i=ker j, im j=ker k and im k=ker i; an initial couple has r=1, and its first spectral page is called E^1.

An initial homological exact couple gives, by repeated derivation, a homological spectral sequence starting at E^1=E with deg d^r=(-r,r-1) and E^r_{p,q} ≅ N^r_{p,q}/B^r_{p,q}, where N^r=k^{-1}(im i^{r-1}) and B^r=j(ker i^{r-1}); no abutment is asserted.
A connection on E is an R-linear map ∇:Γ(E)→Ω¹(M;E)=Γ(Hom(TM,E)) such that ∇(fs)=df⊗s+f∇s for all smooth f and sections s; the definition specifies a given operator, not its existence.

p:E→B has the homotopy lifting property for X if every compatible f:X→E and H:X×I→B admit H̃:X×I→E with H̃(x,0)=f(x) and pH̃=H; a Hurewicz fibration has this for every space, a Serre fibration for every disk D^n, n≥0. Surjectivity is not imposed.

Assume AC. For every space or pair (X,A), abelian group G and n≥0 there is a natural short exact sequence 0→Ext¹_Z(H_{n-1}(X,A;Z),G)→H^n(X,A;G)→Hom_Z(H_n(X,A;Z),G)→0 in which the right map is Kronecker evaluation.

For a first-quadrant double complex, F^col_s T_n = ⊕_{p+q=n, p≤s} C_{p,q} and F^row_s T_n = ⊕_{p+q=n, q≤s} C_{p,q} are filtered subcomplexes; their associated graded components are C_{s,t} (column) and C_{t,s} (row), with no inserted sign.

For a first-quadrant homological double complex C, the row filtration of T=Tot(C) has E^1_{p,q}=H^h_q(C_{*,p}), d^1 induced by v, E^2_{p,q}=H^v_p(H^h_q(C)), page-r differential of bidegree (-r,r-1), and E^∞_{p,q} ≅ F^row_pH_{p+q}(T)/F^row_{p-1}H_{p+q}(T) with the finite image filtration.

For a first-quadrant homological double complex C, the column filtration of T=Tot(C) has E^1_{p,q}=H^v_q(C_{p,*}), d^1 induced by h, E^2_{p,q}=H^h_p(H^v_q(C)), differentials of bidegree (-r,r-1) and E^∞_{p,q} ≅ F^col_pH_{p+q}(T)/F^col_{p-1}H_{p+q}(T).

For an increasingly filtered chain complex in an abelian category, D^1_{p,q}=H_{p+q}(F_pC) and E^1_{p,q}=H_{p+q}(F_pC/F_{p-1}C) form an initial exact couple with maps induced by inclusion, quotient and the homology connecting morphism of degrees (1,-1), (0,0) and (-1,0); no boundedness or completeness is needed.

A spectral sequence converges weakly to a family H_n with increasing filtrations if it has a defined limiting page and specified isomorphisms E^∞_{p,q} ≅ F_pH_{p+q}/F_{p-1}H_{p+q} induced by actual cycles; abstract isomorphism types are insufficient and no completeness or separatedness is asserted.

A spectral sequence converges strongly if it converges weakly, is two-sided regular, and its target filtration is exhaustive, separated and complete (H_n ≅ lim H_n/F_pH_n); all conditions and the weak-convergence identifications are part of the data.

For a based Serre fibration p:(E,e_0)→(B,b_0) with fiber F, the sequence ⋯→π_n(F)→π_n(E)→π_n(B)→∂π_{n-1}(F)→⋯→π_1(B)→∂π_0(F)→π_0(E)→π_0(B) is exact wherever there is an incoming and outgoing arrow; there is a right action of π_1(B) on π_0(F) whose orbits are the fibers of i_*, and ∂_p[γ]=[e_0]·[γ]^{-1}.

For all spaces X,Y the singular shuffle map S:C_•(X;Z)⊗C_•(Y;Z)→C_•(X×Y;Z) is a natural chain homotopy equivalence; a natural inverse and natural homotopies can be specified without AC, and the assertion extends over every commutative unital ring.

Assume AC and R a commutative PID. For spaces X,Y and n≥0 there is a natural short exact sequence 0→⊕_{p+q=n}H_p(X;R)⊗_R H_q(Y;R)→H_n(X×Y;R)→⊕_{p+q=n-1}Tor_1^R(H_p(X;R),H_q(Y;R))→0 whose left map is the singular cross product; no splitting is asserted.

C_k^∞(M;R)=R^{(S_k^∞(M))} (k≥0, zero for k<0) is the subcomplex of the continuous real singular chains spanned by smooth simplices with the same signed face differential, and C_∞^k(M;R)=Hom_R(C_k^∞(M;R),R) with δφ=φ∂; negative groups vanish.

Assume AC_ω. For every smooth manifold M, possibly with boundary, the inclusion of smooth into continuous real singular chains induces an isomorphism H_k^∞(M;R)→H_k^sing(M;R) in every degree, natural for smooth maps; boundary targets are handled by moving a finite compact set into the interior.
Assume AC_ω. For every smooth manifold M, possibly with boundary, restriction induces a natural isomorphism H^k_sing(M;R)≅H_∞^k(M;R) in every integer degree, naturality for smooth maps.

Every supplied smooth Riemannian metric on a smooth manifold, including manifolds with boundary, has exactly one Levi-Civita connection (metric compatible and torsion free); the Koszul construction requires no choice assumption.

For a smooth curve γ:I→M (one-sided data at included endpoints), every t_0∈I and v_0∈E_{γ(t_0)} have exactly one parallel section with V(t_0)=v_0; the same holds for piecewise smooth curves on a compact interval with continuity at the corners, and a singleton carries its prescribed vector.

For a piecewise smooth curve γ:[a,b]→M and v∈E_{γ(a)}, P_γ(v)=V_v(b), where V_v is the unique continuous piecewise parallel section with V_v(a)=v; on a singleton P_γ is the identity and an empty curve is not assigned a map.

Given frames e_α on U_α with e_β=e_αA_{αβ}, matrices ω_α of smooth one-forms are the local matrices of a unique connection if and only if ω_β=A_{αβ}^{-1}ω_αA_{αβ}+A_{αβ}^{-1}dA_{αβ} on every overlap; no local finiteness or choice assumption is required.

A locally trivial fiber bundle is a continuous p:E→B with an open cover (U_i) and homeomorphisms θ_i:p^{-1}(U_i)→U_i×F over U_i; it is numerable when the data include a locally finite partition of unity (ρ_i) with supp(ρ_i)⊆U_i (support-subordinate convention).
For any supplied smooth Riemannian metric, the Koszul expression K determines a unique smooth affine connection by ∇_XY=(½K(X,Y,·))^♯, on manifolds with boundary and without AC.

concerns.concern: The strong-convergence clause is stated in two layers - prose 'bounded above on each total-degree diagonal' and the formal condition that for every k there are a_k>=0 and P_k with E^{a_k}_{s,k-s}=0 for all s>P_k. The proof's crux is step 1.2's uniform primitive bound (from b in F_tC_n cap d(C_{n+1}) with t <= P-a, produce y in F_PC_{n+1} by finite descent), and steps 1.3, 3.2 and 4.1 make countable selections under AC. I followed these steps and found them consistent, but the exact correspondence to Weibel 5.5.10's hypotheses is asserted rather than proved and the diagonal hypothesis is nonstandard; Step-7 should confirm the formal hypothesis is the one actually used and that the AC bookkeeping matches [F8].

The item carries the full construction of the Hom bundle (quotient topology, openness, Hausdorffness, second countability, chart comparison) inside a definition, and some of its central claims are compressed, for example that distinct maps over the same base point have disjoint neighbourhoods inside one open Hom chart. Later items (dual, tensor, Hom, exterior bundles, endomorphism-valued one-forms, Omega^1(M;E)) rely on this smooth interface, so the topological assertions deserve detailed checking.

This lemma, and lem-compatible-smooth-simplex-faces-have-a-neighbourhood-extension before it, import specific construction data (the embedding j, its image S, the open U and the retraction R) from the published proofs of thm-whitney-approximation-for-manifold-valued-maps and thm-relative-whitney-approximation-for-manifold-valued-maps. The latter's library record is an owner repair marked repaired-and-locally-checked with no independent judge (2026-09-10). The whole 9A smoothing chain and thm-smooth-singular-chains-compute-singular-homology inherit the evidential status of those suppliers; the statements themselves matched the suppliers on my reading.

The examples page prose says the examples avoid 'the unresolved general complete-convergence criterion', but the companion page records the 2026-09-10 owner repair and thm-complete-exhaustive-filtered-complex-convergence-criterion is present with a proof; the word 'unresolved' is stale relative to the current files.

The delicate points are the compact-open continuity of lambda_T (step 1.1), the local finiteness of the family {lambda_T} (steps 1.3, 2.1) and the joint continuity of Lambda (step 5.1); the sole AC use is the well-order of the finite chart words. I read the complete argument but did not re-derive these estimates line by line, so Step-7 should line-check them.
